S1.label: Hard to See Clearly
S1.copy: Parts of your current financial picture appear difficult to see clearly right now. When the numbers and the day-to-day flow are hard to follow, it can be difficult to know what deserves attention first.

S2.label: Some Important Gaps
S2.copy: You appear able to see parts of your financial picture, while important gaps remain. More visibility may make it easier to separate what feels urgent from what is actually driving the pattern.

S3.label: Coming Into Focus
S3.copy: Your financial picture appears to be coming into focus. You can identify some of what is happening, while other parts may still require a closer look before the whole picture feels clear.

S4.label: Clear
S4.copy: You are not operating in the dark. You have a solid view of what is happening with your money, where much of it is going, and the patterns that deserve your attention. That visibility matters: you can make a different decision much faster when you can actually see the decision in front of you.

S5.label: Very Clear
S5.copy: You show strong financial visibility. You appear willing and able to look at the numbers, recognize where money is going, and describe the larger picture with confidence.

S1.label: Very Limited Room
S1.copy: There appears to be very little financial room after regular needs and obligations are handled. That is a capacity finding, not a judgment about discipline or effort.

S2.label: Limited Room
S2.copy: After current obligations are handled, there appears to be limited flexibility for multiple priorities at the same time. That can make saving, planning ahead, enjoying life, handling surprises, and pursuing new goals compete for the same dollars. The problem is not necessarily a lack of priorities — it is that too many priorities may be standing in line for too little available room.

S3.label: Some Room
S3.copy: There appears to be some financial room, but it may not feel consistent or sufficient for every priority competing for attention.

S4.label: Meaningful Room
S4.copy: You usually appear to have meaningful room to make choices beyond immediate obligations and can direct some money toward additional priorities.

S5.label: Strong Room
S5.copy: You show strong financial flexibility. After regular needs are handled, you appear to have room to address several priorities without every decision becoming a tradeoff.

S1.label: Mostly Reactive
S1.copy: Financial decisions appear often to be made in response to what needs attention first. A clearer decision process may help you direct available money more deliberately.
S1.source: Q10, Q11, Q12 with capacity overrides

S2.label: Often Reactive
S2.copy: Competing needs can make financial decisions feel reactive. There is room to strengthen how priorities are chosen when money is available to direct.
S2.source: Q10, Q11, Q12 with capacity overrides

S3.label: Developing Direction
S3.copy: Your decision-making appears mixed: some choices are intentional, while others are still shaped by what is most immediate. The pattern is developing rather than fixed.
S3.source: Q10, Q11, Q12 with capacity overrides

S4.label: Intentional
S4.copy: You usually appear to make financial decisions intentionally and can weigh tradeoffs rather than simply responding to the loudest demand.
S4.source: Q10, Q11, Q12 with capacity overrides

S5.label: Highly Intentional
S5.copy: You show a strong pattern of directing available money with purpose. You appear able to decide what money needs to accomplish and make tradeoffs with that purpose in mind.
S5.source: Q10, Q11, Q12 with capacity overrides

S1.label: Highly Exposed
S1.copy: Your responses show that an unexpected expense or major disruption could create significant financial strain. The issue here is resilience: how much protection exists when normal plans are interrupted.

S2.label: Limited Cushion
S2.copy: Recovery from a meaningful disruption could be difficult or could create additional financial problems. Strengthening resilience may deserve attention.

S3.label: Developing Resilience
S3.copy: You have thought about what can go wrong, and you appear capable of handling some financial disruption. The question is what happens when the disruption becomes large enough to outlast a quick adjustment. Your resilience is developing, but a meaningful setback could still place pressure on other parts of your financial life before recovery is complete.

S4.label: Prepared
S4.copy: You appear to have meaningful financial resilience. You have thought about disruptions and appear to have some ability to absorb or recover from them.

S5.label: Strongly Prepared
S5.copy: You show strong preparedness and resilience. You appear to understand major vulnerabilities and have meaningful flexibility or resources for responding when normal plans are disrupted.

S1.label: Destination Unclear
S1.copy: Your responses show that the future your money is meant to support is not yet clearly defined. Without a destination, financial activity can stay busy without becoming directional.
S1.source: Q17, Q18, Q19; Q16 context; Q18 capacity modifier

S2.label: Direction Is Forming
S2.copy: Parts of your financial destination appear to be taking shape, but today's decisions may not yet feel consistently connected to it.
S2.source: Q17, Q18, Q19; Q16 context; Q18 capacity modifier

S3.label: Some Direction
S3.copy: You appear to have some sense of where you want your money to take you, although the connection between that destination and current activity may still be developing.
S3.source: Q17, Q18, Q19; Q16 context; Q18 capacity modifier

S4.label: Clear Direction
S4.copy: You know what you want money to make possible. The destination is not the fuzzy part. The challenge is creating enough room in the present for more of your financial choices to consistently support the future you already have in mind. You do not need a destination invented for you; you need more capacity to move toward the one you already see.
S4.source: Q17, Q18, Q19; Q16 context; Q18 capacity modifier

S5.label: Strongly Directed
S5.copy: You show a strong sense of financial destination. You can describe what you want money to make possible and appear to organize current decisions around that direction.
S5.source: Q17, Q18, Q19; Q16 context; Q18 capacity modifier

S1.label: Information Stalls
S1.copy: Your responses show that financial information often does not make it all the way into action. The friction may occur while sorting information, evaluating it, or following through.

S2.label: Action Often Slows
S2.copy: Useful information can lose momentum before it becomes a decision or consistent action. Identifying where the process slows may be more useful than simply adding more information.

S3.label: Sometimes Moves
S3.copy: Your responses suggest a mixed pattern: some financial information becomes action, while other information remains something you know, consider, or intend to revisit.

S4.label: Usually Moves
S4.copy: Useful information generally does not just sit with you. When something makes sense, you are often able to identify what it means and move toward a decision or next step. That is important because it suggests more information alone may not be the missing ingredient. The bigger question may be whether there is enough financial room for the action you are prepared to take.

S5.label: Moves Into Action
S5.copy: You show a strong information-to-action pattern. You appear able to sort useful information, evaluate it, and move it into decisions and follow-through.

DIRECT_CAPACITY_LIMITED.label: Intentional — Capacity Constrained
DIRECT_CAPACITY_LIMITED.copy: Your answers point to intentional decisions rather than a lack of intentionality. What may be limiting the picture is simpler and less personal: there is too little money left after necessary expenses to make all of the additional decisions you would otherwise make.

DIRECT_LIMITED_EVIDENCE_CAPACITY.label: Limited Evidence
DIRECT_LIMITED_EVIDENCE_CAPACITY.copy: There is not enough clean evidence to make a broad statement about your financial decision style. Why? Because when there is very little money left to direct, it becomes difficult to tell the difference between what you would choose and what your circumstances currently allow you to choose. So this part of your picture deserves some humility: limited financial room should not be mistaken for limited financial agency.

AIM_CAPACITY_CONSTRAINED_ALIGNMENT.label: Clear Direction — Limited Room to Act
AIM_CAPACITY_CONSTRAINED_ALIGNMENT.copy: You know where you want to go, and the destination itself is not the problem. What may be missing is the room: limited financial space can make it difficult for today's decisions to reflect that future as fully as you would like. This is a capacity constraint, not an absence of direction.
